transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m having trouble keeping my mind on one thing. At work, in the warehouse, little things like a beeper or a forklift alarm, or someone moving a pallet, pull me off what I’m doing. Then I look back and I’ve put the wrong numbers into inventory.
Have you had trouble focusing like this before, or is this something that’s new for you?
It’s pretty new, I think. Maybe about a month. It started after my husband stopped working outside the house… our routine changed, and since then I’ve been noticing it more.
Do you find yourself getting distracted or having trouble staying focused on tasks at home, like during conversations or while doing chores, or is this mainly happening at work?

Mostly at work. At home… I mean, I don’t notice it as much. It’s the warehouse stuff that gets me—beepers, alarms, people moving things around—and then I lose my place and mess up the inventory numbers.
Do you find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble staying seated during the day, especially at work?

I don’t know if I’d call it restless exactly. I’ve just been… taking on more than usual. At work I keep starting these safety improvement ideas, and then outside work I’ve signed up for extra art workshops. I’ve been making a lot of lists and schedules, like I’m trying to run everything.
When you're at work, do you find it hard to sit still for long periods, or do you feel like you're constantly moving or switching tasks even when you don't mean to?

Yeah… I guess so. Even after my shifts, I’m not really worn out like I used to be. I come home kind of buzzing, and I’ll start reorganizing cabinets or sorting stuff in the garage. Sitting on the couch just feels… hard.
Have you noticed any days where you felt unusually upbeat, overly energetic, or like you didn’t need much sleep?

Yeah… some days I do feel kind of unusually up, I guess. Like I can get the whole house fixed up and straighten things out at work all in one evening. And then if my husband asks about one of my plans, I can get… sharp with him over nothing.

Have you had a period of time where your mood was really high or irritable, and you were doing a lot more things than usual—like starting a bunch of new projects or feeling like you had extra energy—for at least a week straight?
Yeah… it’s been more than a week. Maybe about a month now, since my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine got thrown off. I guess that’s when it started.

latest_inference.note: The patient has reported a persistent elevated mood, increased activity, decreased need for rest, and engagement in multiple new projects (e.g., safety improvement ideas, art workshops, reorganizing at home) lasting more than a week—likely meeting criteria for a manic episode, which points to Bipolar I Disorder, current episode manic (F31.0). Other candidates like ADHD (F90.0), Major Depressive Disorder (F32.9), and Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.9) are ruled out based on the presence of a manic episode rather than solely inattentive, depressive, or anxiety symptoms.
